science.title: Machine learning enhanced microwave electrometry in many-body Rydberg atoms
science.description: Precision microwave electrometry using Rydberg atoms is limited by many-body interactions at moderate or not too low excitation densities, which may result in distorted probe spectra of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) as predicted by mean-field superatom simulations. This nonlinearity fundamentally restricts measurement accuracy and renders the linear response formula of Autler-Townes splitting to microwave (MW) amplitude inapplicable. Here we present a machine learning (ML) framework assisted by principal component analysis (PCA) that can well overcome this difficulty by mapping distorted noisy EIT spectra directly to MW electric fields. Numerical results show that a basic PCA-assisted regression model reduces the minimal detectable MW field by a few folds as compared to both linear response formula and nonlinear least squares fitting in the interaction-dominant regime. It is of more interest that we can employ a four-class ensemble ML scheme to further reduce the minimal detectable MW field by two orders of magnitude to approach its noise-dependent physical limit and hence largely improve the measurement sensitivity. Our work transforms detrimental Rydberg interactions into beneficial spectral features, providing a practical route toward optimal sensitivity for MW quantum sensing in the nonlinear regime. Rydberg atom-based microwave electrometry is hindered by many-body interactions, distorting probe spectra and limiting measurement accuracy. Here, the authors employ a machine learning framework with principal component analysis to map distorted spectra to microwave fields, significantly enhancing sensitivity and transforming interaction challenges into advantageous spectral features for quantum sensing.

science.title: Using the Stressor-System-Resilience Resources-Outcomes (SSRO) scaffold to clarify the core components of resilience research in medicine
science.description: Modern medicine increasingly extends beyond treating disease to supporting individuals through recovery, adaptation, and long-term functioning, all central to the concept of resilience. Despite growing interest, resilience remains conceptually difficult to structure and compare across disciplines, limiting its value for guiding research and clinical care. In this Perspective, we identify recurring features across many resilience traditions and propose a practical organizing scaffold for studying resilience in medicine. The scaffold specifies four elements that any resilience study should make explicit: the stressor, the system, resilience-relevant resources and processes, and outcomes. Using worked examples, we show how the scaffold clarifies resilience questions and improves comparability across studies. We also provide a step-by-step roadmap to help researchers new to the field design resilience studies, from framing a question through to interpreting results. Ravi et al. propose the SSRO scaffold, identifying four elements, stressor, system, resources, and outcomes, needed to study resilience consistently across medicine. Worked examples from ageing and neurology show how the scaffold clarifies resilience questions, and a step-by-step roadmap guides study design for researchers new to the field.

science.title: Effectiveness of probiotic supplementation in reducing halitosis among older adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial
science.description: Halitosis is a common oral health condition among older adults and is primarily associated with volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) produced by oral bacteria. Probiotics have been proposed as a potential approach to modulate oral microbiota and reduce halitosis. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei TISTR 2688 in reducing halitosis-related parameters in older adults. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial was conducted among 30 older adults with clinically diagnosed halitosis. Participants received either a daily probiotic supplement containing L. paracasei TISTR 2688 or a placebo during two intervention periods. VSC levels, including hydrogen sulfide (H2S), methyl mercaptan (CH3SH), and dimethyl sulfide ((CH3)2S), were measured using Oral Chroma™. Oral health parameters, including plaque index, gingival index, and bleeding index, were assessed at baseline, day 7, and day 14. Data were analyzed using paired statistical tests, with significance set at P < 0.05. All participants (n = 30; 6 males and 24 females; mean age 70.5 ± 4.3 years) completed the study. Compared with baseline, the probiotic intervention significantly reduced plaque index, gingival index, and bleeding index at day 14 (P < 0.05). Significant reductions in VSC levels (H2S, CH3SH, and (CH3)2S) were observed in the probiotic group at both day 7 and day 14 (p < 0.05), whereas no significant changes were found in the placebo group. The reductions in VSC concentrations were substantial, indicating a consistent effect over the intervention period. Supplementation with Lacticaseibacillus paracasei TISTR 2688 was associated with improvements in oral health parameters and reductions in VSC levels in older adults with halitosis. These findings suggest that this probiotic strain may be a useful adjunctive approach for managing halitosis. Further studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up are warranted.

science.title: Associations between early regulatory problems and long-term neurobiological and psychosocial outcomes
science.description: Early regulatory problems (RPs, i.e. problems with crying, sleeping and feeding), are associated with increased susceptibility to avoidant personality traits and peer relationship issues in adulthood. RPs have been linked to intrinsic functional connectivity changes within the allostatic-interoceptive system, notably involving the insula, which integrates sensory and interoceptive signals. The current study investigated whether early RPs and psychosocial outcomes in adulthood are associated with the insula morphology. Using data of the Bavarian Longitudinal Study, we analyzed individuals with RPs (N = 47) and a matched never RPs group (N = 121), who, in adulthood, underwent MRI and completed the Young Adult Self Report and Life Course Interview, to derive avoidant personality and peer relationship quality scores. RP group showed increased gyrification in the left insula when avoidant personality traits were included in the model. Importantly, individuals with both RPs and higher avoidant personality scores exhibited morphological insula differences. No significant associations were observed in cortical volume, thickness, or sulcal depth, or with peer relationship quality. Morphological differences were largest in individuals with persistent RPs. The findings highlight associations between early RPs and long-lasting neurobiological and psychosocial outcomes, providing important insights for the planning and development of targeted prevention and intervention strategies.

science.title: Generation of negative acoustic radiation forces
science.description: Negative acoustic radiation forces act opposite to the direction of wave propagation. While this force reversal has been demonstrated for sub-wavelength particles, achieving it on objects larger than the acoustic wavelength (λ) remains challenging and has typically been demonstrated in limited cases. Expanding on the concept of acoustic pulling, we present a method to generate negative radiation forces on elastic spheres comparable to or larger than λ using a focused multi-element array. Unlike previous demonstrations requiring sources that surround the object or the object to have specific material properties or geometries, we generate tailored acoustic beams that impart negative forces on solid glass spheres positioned 9.5 centimeters away from the transducer’s aperture plane. The beams exhibit an on-axis null region and refocus the pressure behind the sphere, thus minimizing backscatter and enabling the force direction reversal. Experiments and simulations confirm negative radiation forces on spheres with diameters up to 3λ. These results provide a promising framework for developing acoustic tractor beams for non-contact manipulation in environments such as biological benchtop settings, microgravity, and manufacturing.
